# Outliers detection
**To remember:** M values larger than -+16 are very close to 0 or 1 beta values respectively, this mean that those data points are not very useful since are very likely to indicate batch effects or some other technical problems but not biology. If I look the boxplot per sample, I can see that there are some samples with extreme values (EV), thus, larger than -+16. 
There are multiple ways to deal with this:
- Truncate data points: For instance use -+15 as cut-off, all data points above this values are assigned  the value of the cut-off.
- Winsorize (the one I choose).
- Use z-score to reduce the effefct of outliers, but keeping all in.

I can divide the analysis into outlier samples and outlier probes. First, I can start with outlier samples. 

```{r}
m.values <- ENmix::B2M(BMIQ.betas)
boxplot(m.values, main = "M-value distribution across samples")
```




```{r}

# Function to apply winsorization on EPIC array data
winsorize_epic_array <- function(data) {
  # Ensure the data is in a data frame format
  data <- as.data.frame(data)
  
  # Apply winsorization per sample (column-wise)
  winsorized_data <- data %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ {
      # Calculate Q1, Q3, and IQR for the column (CpG-specific)
      Q1 <- quantile(., 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
      Q3 <- quantile(., 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
      IQR <- Q3 - Q1
      
      # Define thresholds for extreme values (EVs)
      lower_threshold <- Q1 - (2 * IQR)
      upper_threshold <- Q3 + (2 * IQR)
      
      # Winsorize values: replace EVs with thresholds
      . <- ifelse(. < lower_threshold, lower_threshold, .)
      . <- ifelse(. > upper_threshold, upper_threshold, .)
      
      return(.)
    }))
  
  return(winsorized_data)
}
```

```{r}
# Apply winsorization
win.m.values <- winsorize_epic_array(m.values)
boxplot(win.m.values, main = "M-value distribution across samples")
```

# Optional for clinical characteristics
To run one-way ANOVA to find significant differences between clinical characteristics e.g
SEO-COPD vs commonCOPD and Controls for age, sex, pack years, etc.

```{r}
df.av <- df_cp_pheno_data %>%
                  mutate(
                  all_groups = ifelse(
                      Group_simple %in% c("MS-COPD", "S-COPD"), "common_COPD", 
                      Group_simple)
                  ) %>% na.omit()

# Ensure BMI is numeric
df.av$BMI <- as.numeric(df.av$BMI)
df.av$Age <- as.numeric(df.av$Age)
df.av$FEV1_FVC_ratio <- as.numeric(df.av$FEV1_FVC_ratio_best)
df.av$FEV1.pred <- as.numeric(df.av$FEV1_percent_of_predicted_best)
df.av$b.cells <- as.numeric(df.av$B.cell.lineage)

# Function to calculate p-values for ANOVA
anova_pvalue <- function(column, group_col) {
  if (is.numeric(df.av[[column]])) {
    model <- aov(df.av[[column]] ~ df.av[[group_col]])
    summary(model)[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]
  } else {
    NA
  }
}

# Run ANOVA for numeric columns
numeric_columns <- c("Age", "BMI", "FEV1_FVC_ratio", "FEV1.pred", "b.cells")
p_values <- sapply(numeric_columns, anova_pvalue, group_col = "all_groups")

# Create a dataframe of p-values
pval_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = numeric_columns,
  p_value = p_values
)

# Add threshold categories
pval_df$Threshold <- cut(
  pval_df$p_value,
  breaks = c(0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
  labels = c("<0.01", "<0.05", "<0.1", ">=0.1"),
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

# Prepare data for heatmap
heatmap_data <- dcast(pval_df, Variable ~ Threshold, value.var = "p_value", fill = 1)

# Visualization using heatmap
heatmap(
  as.matrix(heatmap_data[, -1]),  # Exclude the variable column
  main = "P-value Heatmap for ANOVA",
  color = colorRampPalette(c("red", "yellow", "green"))(50)
)
```






























```{r}
library(ggplot2)
dir.plots.outliers <- file.path(paste0(results.dir, "outliers_detection/plots/")) 
dir.create(dir.plots.outliers, recursive=TRUE)

# Load your data
tBMIQ.betas <- t(BMIQ.betas) # Run on samples

# Run PCA
pca.results <- prcomp(tBMIQ.betas, scale. = TRUE)
exp.var <- pca.results$sdev^2 / sum(pca.results$sdev^2)
cum.var <- cumsum(exp.var)

# Combine proportion and cumulative variance into a data frame
exp.var <- data.frame(
  PC = seq_along(exp.var),
  Proportion = exp.var,
  Cumulative = cumsum(exp.var)
)


filename <- file.path(dir.plots.outliers, "elbow_plot.png")

# Elbow plot
elbow_plot <- ggplot(exp.var[exp.var$PC < 11,]
, aes(x = PC, y = Proportion)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "blue") + # Larger points for emphasis
  geom_line(group = 1, color = "blue", size = 1) + # Thicker line for visibility
  theme_classic() + # Cleaner, professional theme
  labs(
    title = "Elbow Plot: Variance Explained by Principal Components",
    x = "Principal Component (PC)",
    y = "Proportion of Variance Explained"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = exp.var$PC) + # Ensure all PCs are shown
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), # Center title
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"), # Bold axis titles
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12), # Readable axis labels
    #panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray", linetype = "dashed"), # Light grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank() # Remove minor grid lines
  )

# Display the plot
print(elbow_plot)

# Save the plot for publication
ggsave(
  filename = filename, # File name
  plot = elbow_plot,           # Plot to save
  dpi = 300,                   # High resolution
  width = 8, height = 6,       # Dimensions in inches
  units = "in"                 # Units for width and height
)
```

# Hierarchical clustering on PC embedding

```{r}
pca_data <- as.data.frame(pca.results$x[,1:2]) 
# Compute the distance matrix on the PCA-transformed data
dist_matrix <- dist(pca_data, method = "euclidean")

# Perform hierarchical clustering using the "complete" linkage method
hc <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "complete")

png(file.path(dir.plots.outliers, "dendogram_pca_outliers.png"))
# Plot the dendrogram
plot(hc,
     main = "Hierarchical Clustering on PCA",
     xlab = "Samples",
     ylab = "Height",
     labels=FALSE
     )

clusters <- cutree(hc, k = 5)
pca_data$clusters <- as.factor(clusters)

#sample.scores <- pca.results$x[, 1:20]
pheno.data <- data.frame(ENmixMSet@colData)
pheno.data2 <- merge(pheno.data, pca_data, by = "row.names")
rownames(pheno.data2) <- pheno.data2$Row.names

# draw dendogram with red borders around the 5 clusters 
rect.hclust(hc, k=5, border="red")
dev.off()

```

## Probe outliers detection
Check variance distribution, one way is to get e.g top 50000 most variable probes, run PCA. 

```{r}
cpg_variances <- apply(BMIQ.betas, 1, var)

# Step 2: Order the CpG sites by variance in descending order
sorted_indices <- order(cpg_variances, decreasing = TRUE)

# Step 3: Reorder the methylation data matrix based on sorted indices
BMIQ.betas.sorted <- BMIQ.betas[sorted_indices, ]

# Optional: Add variance values as an additional column for reference
betas.val.sorted <- cbind(BMIQ.betas.sorted,
                            Variance = cpg_variances[sorted_indices]
                            )

betas <- betas.val.sorted[, -ncol(betas.val.sorted)]

# View the top rows of the sorted data
head(betas)

```

### Detect outliers

```{r}
pca <- prcomp(
  betas[1:100000,],
  center = TRUE,
  scale = TRUE
)

pca_data <- as.data.frame(pca$x[,1:2]) 


#sample.scores <- pca.results$x[, 1:20]
pheno.data <- data.frame(ENmixMSet@colData)
pheno.data2 <- merge(pheno.data, pca_data, by = "row.names")
rownames(pheno.data2) <- pheno.data2$Row.names


d <- data.frame(PC1 = pca$x[, 1], PC2 = pca$x[, 2])
d
```


```{r}
# CpGs
hvCpGs <- betas[1:100000,]

Q1.Q3 <- apply(hvCpGs, 1 , function(x) quantile(x, probs=c(0.25,0.75), na.rm=TRUE))
IQR.value <- Q1.Q3["75%",] - Q1.Q3["25%",]
lower.fence <- Q1.Q3["25%",] - 3*IQR.value
upper.fence <- Q1.Q3["75%",] + 3*IQR.value

flag <- hvCpGs < lower.fence | hvCpGs > upper.fence 
hvCpGs[flag] <- NA

# CpGs with more than 5% missing values 
rows.na <- rowSums(is.na(hvCpGs)/ncol(hvCpGs))
outliers <- hvCpGs[rows.na > 0.05,]
cpgs <- rownames(outliers)

length(cpgs)
```

```{r}
d$outliers <- ifelse(rownames(d) %in% cpgs, "highlight", "default")

ggplot(d, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = outliers)) +
   geom_point(size = 1) +
   labs(
     title = "PCA top100000 highest variance",
     x = "PC1",
     y = "PC2"
   ) +
   scale_color_manual(
     values = c("highlight" = "red", "default" = "grey")  # Define custom colors
   ) +
   theme_bw() +
   theme(
     plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
     axis.text = element_text(size = 18),
     legend.text = element_text(size = 16)
   )

```

Conclusion
I dont remove the CpGs flag as outliers
